text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] control-plane 5xx spike detected (5xx rate +18% over 3m). Primary source: auth-service -> org-lookup RPC errors. Affected regions: us-east-1, us-west-2. Error signature: orgLookupTimeout/502. Trigger: 2026-03-15T12:03:44Z. Paging on-call (maria)

maria: i'm on it. paging eng-sre / leo, also pinging product for potential customer impact. i'll gather quick scope.

leo: oncall leo here. can someone grab recent auth-service logs and traces? try: 
```
kubectl -n controlplane logs deploy/auth-service --since=10m | grep -i "orgLookup" | tail -n 200
```
will also check trace samples in jaeger for the 12:02-12:06 window.

anne: quick note: we pushed a config-service patch ~12:00 that changed org-lookup concurrency and TTL. i'm seeing increased 5xx from config-service -> auth vote. could be config regression causing upstream timeouts.

maria: customer-facing impact: current estimate ~12% of control-plane requests are 5xx, which maps to ~3% of total API requests. a handful of high-volume customers (company-xyz, analytics-inc) seeing elevated errors in their metrics. putting this as P1.

leo: logs from auth-service (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T12:02:58Z ERROR orgLookup timeout id=0x7f8a3f3 caller=org-client.go:129 err="timeout after 1.5s"
2026-03-15T12:03:01Z WARN  upstream config-service returned 502 id=0x7f8a41b
2026-03-15T12:03:05Z ERROR failed to fetch org for user=U12345 err="rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
```

leo: this looks like a fanout / heartbeat issue where org-lookup calls are backed up and hitting auth timeouts, cascading 5xx. we should reduce fanout and enable fallback cache immediately.

anne: i can flip the gateway circuit-breaker to limit concurrent org-lookup requests and enable cached responses for 2m TTL. suggestion: set gateway.dynamic.config.orgLookup.max_concurrency=20 and gateway.dynamic.config.orgLookup.cacheTTL=120s.

maria: do it. also, can we roll back the config-service deploy if we confirm it caused the regression?

dinesh: i see the config-service deploy id `cfg-deploy-20260315-1200` in the rollout history. i'm prepping a rollback command. if we flip the gateway config first we might buy enough time.

anne: applying gateway change now (updating dynamic config).

opsbot: dynamic-config: update applied by anne to gateway: {"orgLookup.max_concurrency":20,"orgLookup.cacheTTL":120} (version: v2026-03-15-1207) :white_check_mark:

leo: after gateway change, sampling metrics: 5xx rate dropped from +18% -> +9% within 60s. latency tail also improved for org-lookup. still seeing periodic spikes from config-service.

dinesh: rolling back config-service to previous stable `cfg-deploy-20260314-2330` now. command: `rdwctl deploy rollback config-service --to cfg-deploy-20260314-2330`

opsbot: deploy: rollback started by dinesh for config-service -> target cfg-deploy-20260314-2330. CI checks passing.

opsbot: deploy: rollback completed successfully. (duration 47s) :rocket:

maria: monitoring dashboards — control-plane 5xx now at +4% (down from +18%). customer-impact estimate revised to ~0.8% of total API requests. notifying CS and our top affected customers.

leo: action items while stabilized:
- increase local org-lookup cache TTL by default for 24h
- add backpressure in org-lookup client (client-side rate limiting)
- add circuit-breaker on config-service calls
- postmortem to include why deploy didn't show in canary metrics

anne: filing a quick mitigation PR to persist gateway defaults (will follow up).

maria: handing off incident to night on-call (dinesh) at 13:00 UTC for monitoring and follow-ups. handoff notes: rollback completed, gateway concurrency lowered, cacheTTL increased to 120s, tune client-side backoff needed. if 5xx creeps above 5% re-page eng-sre.

dinesh: ack. will keep watch and start triage items. leaving a pager note for oncall rotation.

maria: thanks all — great quick run. i'll open the incident ticket and assign owners for the action items (postmortem + defaults + improvements). :heart:

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared. Follow-up required: postmortem, canary threshold tuning, circuit-breaker defaults.

[reactions: maria :thumbsup:, leo :eyes:, anne :white_check_mark:, dinesh :raised_hands:]
